question: A urine screen flags opiates in a woman who ate a poppy-seed bagel. Rerun, the same screen flags again. What does that add?
options: Little: same test, same blind spot
A lot: two positives confirm it
answer: Little. Poppy seeds carry real traces of morphine and codeine, and the screening test reads them the same way every time. Confirmation needs a different method, such as mass spectrometry, and a cut-off set above what seeds give. US federal workplace testing raised its morphine cut-off from 300 to 2,000 nanograms per millilitre in 1998.
move: A second check only counts if it could fail in a different way.
ask: When I double-check something, am I using a different route, or just asking the same source twice?
trap: A lot: two positives confirm it, as two votes beat one.
source: Moeller et al., Mayo Clinic Proceedings, 2008
reference: Moeller, Lee & Kissack, Urine drug screening: practical guide for clinicians, Mayo Clinic Proceedings, 2008
